result.judge_notes: pass 1 (A=with, B=without): Both answers find the six-family overload, the similar sans faces, the Courier phone number and Playfair's thin strokes, and both give a concrete two-family replacement. B handles older readers better, with advice on 18px body text, line-height, contrast and tappable tel: links, but it says 'four similar sans-serifs' while naming only three and says nothing about fallbacks or font loading. A gives a real fallback stack and a short note on loading and licensing, which wins it the comparison, though its opening line wrongly says each family has a different job. | pass 2 (A=without, B=with): Both answers spot the six competing families, the near-duplicate sans faces and the Courier phone number. Each also gives a concrete smaller set of fonts with a clear role for each. B wins because it covers fallbacks and font loading with real system alternatives, which A leaves out entirely. A gives more practical readability advice for older patients, such as a minimum body size, line-height and tel: links, but it has a small error: it says 'four similar sans-serifs' and then names only three.
